Sharma and Zhang (2004) DBH–height models for Ontario jack pine and black spruce

Source: R/hd_sharmazhang2004.R
hd_sharmazhang2004.Rd

Vectorized implementation of the individual-tree height–diameter models of Sharma and Zhang (2004) for jack pine and black spruce in northern Ontario. Predicts total tree height (m) from DBH (cm), optionally with stand basal area and stand density.

Usage

hd_sharmazhang2004(
  DBH,
  species,
  variant = c("eq2", "eq5"),
  BA = NULL,
  TPH = NULL,
  keep_model_id = FALSE
)

Arguments

DBH

Numeric vector. Tree level. Diameter at breast height (1.3 m above ground), in cm. Must be >= 0.

species

Character vector. Tree level. NFI species codes ("PINU.BAN" or "PICE.MAR"; compact "PINUBAN" is accepted).

variant

Model variant: "eq2" (default; DBH, BA and TPH) or "eq5" (DBH only).

BA

Numeric vector. Plot level. Total stand basal area (m²/ha) of all trees in the plot, all species (source "BA", "total tree basal area", p. 443). Must be > 0. Required by variant = "eq2".

TPH

Numeric vector. Plot level. Stand density (stems/ha) "of the trees with DBH \(\ge\) 2.5 cm" (source "SD", p. 443). Must be > 0. Required by variant = "eq2".

keep_model_id

Logical. If TRUE, add column model_id ("sharmazhang2004_eq2" or "sharmazhang2004_eq5").

Value

A tibble with column height (m) and, if keep_model_id = TRUE, model_id.

Details

Model scope (species coverage): jack pine (PINU.BAN) and black spruce (PICE.MAR). Fitted to permanent growth study plots (400 m²) across much of northern Ontario; trees of natural and planted origin were both included (p. 443).

Variants (chosen with variant; Tables 3 and 4, p. 445):

  • "eq2" (default): eq. (2), p. 444, the model the source recommends $$H = 1.3 + \alpha \, BA^{\delta} [1 - \exp(-\beta \, TPH^{\phi} \, DBH)].$$

  • "eq5": eq. (5), p. 444, the DBH-only Chapman–Richards model (form of Peng et al. 2001, refitted by the source) $$H = 1.3 + \alpha [1 - \exp(-\beta \, DBH)]^{\gamma}.$$

Eqs. (3) and (4) are not implemented: with the published coefficients they predict a height that does not change with DBH.

Height convention: total tree height; the 1.3 m breast height is added so that predicted height equals 1.3 m when DBH is 0 (p. 444).

Fit: ordinary (unweighted) nonlinear least squares; there are no random effects, so the predictions are the published fixed curves.

Rows with NA in any input used by the variant return NA height. Inputs outside the per-species range of the data (DBH, Table 2; plot BA and stems/ha, Table 1) are computed and reported in a single warning.

References

Sharma, M., and Zhang, S.Y. (2004). Height–diameter models using stand characteristics for Pinus banksiana and Picea mariana. Scandinavian Journal of Forest Research, 19(5), 442–451. doi:10.1080/02827580410030163

See also

hd_model_registry(), get_hd_model_info()

Examples

hd_sharmazhang2004(
  DBH = c(10, 20, 30),
  species = c("PINU.BAN", "PICE.MAR", "PICE.MAR"),
  BA = 25, TPH = 1500
)
#> # A tibble: 3 × 1
#>   height
#>    <dbl>
#> 1   19.0
#> 2   20.2
#> 3   24.4

# DBH only
hd_sharmazhang2004(DBH = c(10, 20, 30), species = "PINU.BAN", variant = "eq5")
#> # A tibble: 3 × 1
#>   height
#>    <dbl>
#> 1   9.43
#> 2  16.0 
#> 3  20.8 

# Inside dplyr::mutate() with tree and plot data
trees <- data.frame(
  DBH = c(12, 25, 18),
  species = c("PINU.BAN", "PICE.MAR", "PICE.MAR"),
  BA = c(30, 30, 18), TPH = c(3000, 3000, 1200)
)
dplyr::mutate(trees, hd_sharmazhang2004(DBH, species, BA = BA, TPH = TPH))
#>   DBH  species BA  TPH   height
#> 1  12 PINU.BAN 30 3000 20.18434
#> 2  25 PICE.MAR 30 3000 22.54408
#> 3  18 PICE.MAR 18 1200 18.05406
